The Constant of a Multivariate t and Its Derivatives in nu

Source: R/mvstudent_t_distrib.R
mvt_cp_d.Rd

Computes the \(k\)-th derivative of \(c_p(\nu) = \log\Gamma\{(\nu+p)/2\} - \log\Gamma(\nu/2) - (p/2)\log\nu\), for \(k\) from 0 to 4, without the cancellation of the direct form: every derivative vanishes as \(\nu\) grows, while the terms of the direct form do not.

Usage

mvt_cp_d(nu, p, k)

Arguments

nu

The degrees of freedom, a numeric vector of positive values.

p

The dimension, a single positive whole number.

k

The order of the derivative, 0 to 4.

Value

A numeric vector as long as nu.

Details

For even \(p\) the recurrence of the gamma function telescopes into $$c_p(\nu) = -\tfrac{p}{2}\log 2 + \sum_{j=1}^{p/2-1} \log\!\left(1 + \tfrac{2j}{\nu}\right),$$ whose derivatives are \((-1)^{k-1}(k-1)!\,\nu^{-k}\sum_j \{(1 + 2j/\nu)^{-k} - 1\}\), in which each term is formed with base::expm1() and base::log1p(). For odd \(p\) and \(\nu \ge \max(20, 4p)\) the series of mvt_nu_coef() is summed, $$c_p^{(k)}(\nu) = (-1)^{k-1}\sum_{n \ge 1} g_n \frac{(n+k-1)!}{\nu^{n+k}}, \qquad c_p(\nu) = -\tfrac{p}{2}\log 2 - \sum_{n \ge 1} g_n \frac{(n-1)!}{\nu^n};$$ below that bound the direct form in base::lgamma() and base::psigamma() is used, where it keeps its digits.

See also

mvt_h_d() for the part of the log-density that carries the data, mvt_A(), which is twice its first derivative, and mvt_nu_coef() for the series.

Examples

nu <- c(5, 50, 1e6)
# The result is compared with the direct form, which loses its digits as
# nu grows.
rbind(exact = distributions7:::mvt_cp_d(nu, 3, 0L),
      direct = lgamma((nu + 3) / 2) - lgamma(nu / 2) - 1.5 * log(nu))
#>              [,1]      [,2]     [,3]
#> exact  -0.9070803 -1.024918 -1.03972
#> direct -0.9070803 -1.024918 -1.03972
